requirements.statement: Add a package-owned official AIDLC bundle resolver that selects installed-package, managed-payload, or source-checkout resources by deterministic precedence; validates outer package and inner bundle integrity without current-working-directory or network dependence; returns a typed fingerprinted receipt with truthful trust posture; and fails closed without mutating unsafe or conflicting state.

path_bindings.ownership_evidence: The Phase 2 design assigns the typed multi-provider resolver to a package-owned module; repository inspection found only generic resource verification and script-local validators, not an existing package resolver.

proof_bindings.asserted_behavior: Provider discovery, precedence, path safety, inventory comparison, and receipt fingerprinting are deterministic pure or filesystem-bounded behaviors.
The resolver receipt exposes the required provider identity, official identity, trust posture, artifact identity, bundle fingerprint, verified root, network posture, issues, and stable fingerprint.

Installed-package, managed-payload, and source-checkout fixtures resolve independently of the current working directory, use no network, report truthful distinct trust postures, and leave invalid state untouched.

positive: All three package resource providers resolve through one typed package-owned contract with deterministic precedence and no current-working-directory dependency.
A successful receipt binds the selected provider, official identity, verified bundle root, integrity fingerprints, trust posture, artifact-identity status, and network_used false.
Missing, altered, incompatible, incomplete, unsafe, or conflicting inputs return categorized fail-closed results without writes.
negative: Local hashes or self-authored manifests never become authenticated-release authority.
Resolution never accesses the network, executes pack content, follows unsafe links, mutates provider state, creates project projections, or changes Full routing.
Legacy schema-v1 state is never promoted or accepted as authority for a new Full run.

requirements.statement: Extend generic package resource handling only as needed to expose safe module-relative bundle locations and exact outer package-integrity evidence to the shared resolver, while preserving existing package verification behavior.

proof_bindings.asserted_behavior: Package-root and bundle-location helpers remain module-relative and reject unsafe or incomplete package inventory.
Outer integrity evidence is explicit and cannot be confused with authenticated artifact identity.
Changing the process working directory does not change the resolved package bundle or its integrity decision.

positive: The resolver receives safe module-relative package locations and exact package-integrity findings.
negative: Generic package resource verification is not weakened, duplicated, or made current-working-directory dependent.

requirements.statement: Refactor the read-only official AIDLC compatibility detector into an adapter over the shared resolver so status reports provider identity and trust posture consistently while retaining bounded legacy schema-v1 inspection and existing negative integrity behavior.

proof_bindings.asserted_behavior: Detector rendering and compatibility mapping consume the resolver receipt without mutating state.
The status payload preserves legacy bounded inspection fields and adds the canonical provider and trust-posture projection.
Valid schema-v2 bundle status succeeds read-only; altered, incompatible, unsafe, or legacy-new-Full authority cases fail closed consistently with the shared resolver.

positive: The public read-only detector delegates to one shared resolver result and exposes provider identity plus truthful trust posture.
negative: The adapter neither mutates state nor lets schema-v1 project packs authorize new Full execution.
